title: Cheaper turns: a fast gate and scripts instead of bookkeeping

C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified, no design choice

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, clear spec, one or two owned files and their tests

C3.rule: Cross-module design; changes a gate or the ledger contract; wrong means every project inherits it

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, anything in a project's real data, a sponsor decision

items.title: The suite's slowest file stops rebuilding its world per test
items.what: tests/test_warmup.py builds a git repo plus three bin/tracker subprocesses in every test's setUp: 574.9s for 122 tests (finding 23/F-06). Build the seeded project once and copytree it per test. No assertion changes.
items.done: test_warmup's wall clock measured before and after on the same commit, with an unchanged `Ran N tests` line.

parts.title: Build the seeded project once, copy it per test

log.event: Fixture built once and copied per test: Project() falls to 0.03s, template 0.35s once. Honest result: only 7% of the file (TestCardV2Lines 59.2s -> 54.9s, twice). The 4.7s per test was never the fixture -- it is the tests' own bin/warmup calls at 1.9s each.

items.title: The merge gate runs the parallel runner that already exists
items.what: bin/quiet --jobs was built for 23/M-01 and never wired in (finding 23/F-07). Shards dispatch longest-known-first from a duration cache, --jobs auto resolves to cpu_count()-2, and .common-rules.json's gates.merge plus bin/land pass it.
items.done: Serial vs --jobs auto wall clock measured on the same commit after O-01; gates.merge and bin/land use it; the verdict line's shape is unchanged.

items.title: No waiting on a gate: one blocking call, one verdict line
items.what: An agent that backgrounds a gate and polls it spends a full context re-send (~134k tokens, measured) per check to learn nothing. The standard says: run the gate in the foreground, read the verdict line in the same turn, never park a turn on a timer. Mandatory Standard change, in the brief template, the lead prompt and CLAUDE-workflow.md.
items.done: A Standard change (mandatory) CHANGELOG entry; the rule in templates/brief.md, templates/lead-prompt.md and CLAUDE-workflow.md; a test that fails if the brief template loses it.

log.event: Extended the gate rule into CLAUDE-workflow.md's gate section, templates/lead-prompt.md §2 and templates/brief.md's MUST section; CHANGELOG carries the mandatory Standard change entry; tests pin it in tests/test_templates.py

items.title: bin/commit-if-green: gate, verdict and commit in one call
items.what: Today a builder reads the gate's verdict, then issues git add, git commit and git push as separate tool calls -- four model turns for a mechanical sequence, and the OK/FAILED check is applied by the model rather than by code. One wrapper runs the gate, commits and pushes only on a verdict line matching ^OK with no ^FAILED, and reports what it did.
items.done: Refuses on FAILED, on a non-zero exit and on an empty verdict; commits nothing in either case; tested against a fixture repo with a passing and a failing gate.

log.event: Built bin/commit-if-green: runs the gate through bin/quiet, commits and pushes only when quiet's verdict line starts "quiet: OK" and quiet's own exit code is 0. Refuses before running anything on bad usage, --push to main, a merge/rebase in progress, or nothing to commit; treats FAILED, a nonzero exit, or an empty/unrecognised verdict line as failure -- never as success. tests/test_commit_if_green.py (15 cases) against throwaway repos with a fake gate. Evidence: commit sha pending (recorded after push).
Recorded evidence: commit 3a59e5c on branch o04-commit-if-green.
log.evidence: commit 3a59e5c on branch o04-commit-if-green: bin/commit-if-green + tests/test_commit_if_green.py (16 cases, python3 -m unittest test_commit_if_green test_quiet -q ran green -- narrow set, since affected_tests.py names two dozen modules only because the ledger json changed, not because the tool touches them)

items.title: A PR body drafted from the ledger item and the diff
items.what: The lead composes every PR title and body from memory of the item and the diff, having already read both. A script prints a skeleton -- item id, title, files touched, test counts -- for the lead to edit rather than compose.
items.done: Prints a usable body for a real branch and item; the lead's edits are what lands; tested on a fixture ledger and diff.

log.event: bin/pr-body prints a PR title and body skeleton (item what/done/parts, diff counts against --base, branch commits, an unfilled Gate: line, trailer) from tools/itemfacts.py, shared with O-06; commit d15ecd6.

items.title: One draft for the ruflo-item done note and the ledger event
items.what: The same facts (item id, commit, PR, test counts) are written twice by hand: once as the ruflo-item done summary, once as tracker set --event text. Draft both from the same source; the lead adjusts wording.
items.done: Both texts drafted from one call on a fixture item; the lead's wording still wins; tested.

log.event: bin/item-notes drafts the ruflo-item done summary and the tracker set --event sentence from the same tools/itemfacts.py facts as O-05, in the voice real log entries already use, marked as drafts; --commit/--pr appear only when given; commit d15ecd6.

items.title: Batch dispatch: one message carries every unblocked brief
items.what: Six briefs in one message cost one lead turn; six messages cost six. The standard already says to spawn every unblocked C1/C2 item in one message -- say it as a cost rule, with the same rule for reviewing branches, and say that a lead never sends a brief a turn at a time.
items.done: Standard change (mandatory) entry; the rule in the lead prompt and CLAUDE-workflow.md; a test pinning it in the templates.

log.event: Extended batch dispatch as a cost rule into templates/lead-prompt.md §3 and CLAUDE-workflow.md's Issues section; CHANGELOG carries the mandatory Standard change entry; tests pin it in tests/test_templates.py

items.title: A staging branch, so main is never red
items.what: The sponsor: "We can also reduce the number of tests so we can have a development branch or a staging branch where we can keep merging changes and then after a considerable amount of changes are done, we can test in one go." Reviewed branches merge into staging; the full suite runs there, not on main; main fast-forwards from staging only when staging is green. No test is deleted -- what is reduced is the number of runs, not the coverage (finance-tracker had 1,753 green tests over 16 wrong-money defects).
items.done: bin/land knows the staging target; the standard says where the full suite runs and when main advances; a red staging branch cannot reach main; tested on a fixture repo.

items.title: Warm-up stops shelling out 23 times to measure conformance
items.what: Finding 31/F-01: bin/warmup costs 1.9s, of which 1.21s is bin/conformance measure running 23 subprocesses. Every session pays it at startup and test_warmup pays it 122 times. The 23 checks are independent reads -- import them in-process, or run them concurrently, or both. Same verdicts, same output, faster.
items.done: bin/warmup's wall clock measured before and after on the same commit; conformance reports identical verdicts for the same repo state; the 12-check suite stays green.

items.title: Shards split within a file, not just between files
items.what: Finding 31/F-02: bin/quiet shards by test file, so the suite's floor is its slowest file however many cores are free -- which is why --jobs 8 measured 610s. Shard by test class (or by an even split of test ids) so one 575s file spreads across cores.
items.done: The slowest file's tests run across several processes; aggregated counts still match a sequential run; --jobs 8 measured against serial on the same commit.
